annotations.text:
The front door in four beats:

1. The hook, your words — got a good ear, join and prove it.
2. What you actually do — rate to decide who gets promoted; predict to earn points and a shot at the $500.
3. TRY ONE. A stranger plays a real record and finds out how close they were, before signing up for anything.
4. The real question — knowing good music vs knowing the market.

One action, repeated three times: Join the A&R Team.

Two shared components, mounted into BOTH landing artboards — edit here and both update.

Try one runs the REAL scoring curve, so a stranger's first number is what they would actually have earned; the three records already ran, so the average is a settled fact.

The board is YESTERDAY'S, not the cumulative series board. 12,480 tells a stranger they are months behind; 784 tells them they could have done that — and 'everyone starts over at noon' is the line that turns a hierarchy into an invitation.

Needs a `daily.board` field on /api/home. Not new logic: the overlay's default scope and cardArsData(sessionId) already rank participants within one session.

No 'past champions' block — winners[] is still hardcoded empty on the server.

The day is VARIABLE — 4 drawn at random from the free pool plus UP TO 12 paid, so 4 to 16 records. It only reaches 16 when the paid queue is full or backlogged.

Nothing anywhere hardcodes a count. Every artboard with a day on it carries a 'records' tweak — drag it from 4 to 16 and the hero number, the queue rail, the 'Record n of N' line, the completion screen and the landing page all follow.

Server side matches: the completion-bonus denominator is a live COUNT of the day's rounds, so deleting a record shrinks the day rather than stranding anyone one short.

Nothing on this screen exists before the 9:00 AM tally. During the window there is no average, no split and no per-record vote count anywhere in the payload — a count across 21 hours is a popularity signal, which is direction-adjacent.
